Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.

1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2.

The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.13 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 304B, 504,
506, 201 IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station Motiganj, District Gonda.
3. In terms of the FIR, it was alleged that the daughter of the informant was married to the son of the applicant in the year 2018.
Subsequently, an information was received that the daughter of the informant had died and the funeral was also performed.

sentences.text: The Counsel for the applicant argues that the applicant is the mother-in-law of the deceased and she is aged about 58 years.
He further argues that in terms of the medical report on record, prima facie, the victim is tentatively suffering from coronary artery diseases and that was the cause of death.
There is no postmortem report as the funeral was already been.
5. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

6. Considering the material on record coupled with the fact that even in the FIR, there is no specific assertion to the effect that soon before her death, the victim was subjected to any physical or mental harassment at the instance of the applicant in relation to any demand of dowry; the applicant has no criminal antecedents and is languishing in jail since 12.01.2024, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Rani Mishra be released on bail in the aforesaid first information report on her furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which she is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
